## Description {#details}

Utility functions for advanced string handling in tests.

The µTest++ framework includes a collection of utility functions designed to simplify advanced string operations commonly required during test development. These functions support tasks such as partial string matching, splitting long strings for improved readability, and other manipulations that enhance the clarity and effectiveness of test code.

<SectionDefinition>

## Functions

### is&#95;match() {#gaa2f0f4cff320a783ad2347c9ff3fc731}

<MemberDefinition
  prototype={<>bool micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::utility::is&#95;match (std::string&#95;view input, std::string&#95;view pattern)</>}
  labels = {["nodiscard"]}>
Check if a string matches a pattern.

<ParametersList title="Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="[in] input">The string view to be checked.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="[in] pattern">The string view containing the pattern to match.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>

<SectionUser title="Returns">
<code>true</code> if the input string matches the pattern; otherwise, <code>false</code>.
</SectionUser>

This function enables pattern-based string comparison for tests, supporting both exact matches and wildcard patterns. The pattern may include <code>&#42;</code> to match any sequence of characters and <code>?</code> to match any single character. This allows for flexible validation of string content in test assertions, accommodating variable or partially known values.

<ParametersList title="Template Parameters">

<ParametersList title="Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="[in] t">The object from which to remove const qualification.</ParametersListItem>

<SectionUser title="Returns">

The <code>mut</code> function template provides a safe and generic mechanism to remove the <code>const</code> qualifier from any type. It returns a non-const reference to the input object, enabling modification of objects that were originally declared as <code>const</code>. This utility is particularly useful in testing scenarios where controlled mutation of test data is required.

### split() {#ga1b860aa64be17658d1664de447e6e125}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T, class Delim&#95;T&gt;</>}
  prototype={<>std::vector&lt; T &gt; micro&#95;os&#95;plus::micro&#95;test&#95;plus::utility::split (T input, Delim&#95;T delim)</>}

Split a string into a vector of sub-strings.

<ParametersList title="Template Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="T">Type of the input string.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="Delim&#95;T">Type of the delimiter.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>

<ParametersList title="Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="[in] input">Input string to split.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="[in] delim">Delimiter string.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>

<SectionUser title="Returns">
A vector containing the resulting sub-strings.
</SectionUser>

This function template facilitates string handling in tests by splitting a string into a vector of substrings, using the specified delimiter.

The function iterates through the input string, identifying delimiter positions and extracting substrings between them. Each resulting substring is added to the output vector. This approach supports flexible parsing of delimited data, which is particularly useful for validating string processing logic in test cases.
